cards.front: State the two postulates of special relativity that lead to Lorentz transformations.
cards.back: 1. Laws of physics are identical in all inertial frames. 2. Speed of light c is constant in all inertial frames and independent of source motion.

cards.front: Why must coordinate transformations between inertial frames be linear?
cards.back: Linearity ensures constant relative velocity (no acceleration) and that the origin of one frame moves at constant speed in the other; nonlinear terms would violate inertial-frame conditions.

cards.front: Assume $x'=\gamma(x-vt)$, $t'=\gamma(t-\alpha x)$. Using light-speed invariance, find $\gamma$ and $\alpha$.
cards.back: For light $x=ct$ implies $x'=ct'$. Substituting yields $\alpha=v/c^2$ and $\gamma=1/\sqrt{1-v^2/c^2}$.

cards.front: Write the complete set of Lorentz transformations for a boost along x with velocity v.
Derive the inverse Lorentz transformations by swapping v → −v.
Show that the Lorentz transformations reduce to the Galilean transformations when $v\ll c$.
Using the Lorentz transformations, derive the time-dilation formula for a clock at rest in the moving frame.
cards.back: Proper time interval $\Delta\tau=\Delta t'$ at fixed x' gives $\Delta t=\gamma\Delta\tau$.

cards.front: What happens to the Lorentz factor $\gamma$ as $v\to c$? What physical consequence follows?
cards.back: $\gamma\to\infty$. Infinite energy is required to accelerate a massive particle to c; simultaneity and lengths become undefined across frames.
